quests.sentence: She is not available.
quests.hint: Not slots in right after the be-verb, before whatever describes the subject.
quests.explanation: Not follows is directly, between the verb and the complement available — this is the standard negative position with be.

quests.sentence: They are not ready.
quests.hint: The same rule applies with are: the negative word sits right after it.
quests.explanation: Not comes immediately after are, keeping the be-verb and its negative together before the complement ready.

quests.sentence: I am not familiar with this software.
quests.hint: Even with a longer ending, am not still keeps not directly after the verb.
quests.explanation: Am not stays together right after I, and the longer phrase familiar with this software simply follows as the complement.

quests.sentence: The printer isn't working.
quests.hint: Isn't already contains 'is' and 'not' fused together — treat it as one single word.
quests.explanation: Isn't is a contraction of is not and functions as one unit, sitting in the normal be-verb position between the subject and the complement.

quests.sentence: These figures aren't accurate.
quests.hint: Aren't works the same way — one word standing in for are not.
quests.explanation: Aren't fuses are and not into a single word, occupying the same slot a full form would between the plural subject and complement.

quests.sentence: The signal isn't reliable in this building.
quests.hint: The contracted verb still leads the complement, even when a place phrase follows.
quests.explanation: Isn't still comes right after signal, and in this building (a place phrase) simply extends the sentence after the complement reliable.

quests.sentence: She does not agree with the proposal.
quests.hint: Does not stays together as a unit, right after the subject and before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Does not follows she and precedes the base verb agree — the main verb loses its -s ending once does carries it.

quests.sentence: They do not accept late returns.
quests.hint: Do not works the same way with a plural subject, keeping the base verb after it.
quests.explanation: Do not follows they, and accept stays in base form, with late returns completing the object.

quests.sentence: The company does not disclose its revenue.
quests.hint: A possessive word inside the object doesn't change where does not sits.
quests.explanation: Does not follows the company, and disclose stays in base form, with its revenue (including a possessive) as the object.

quests.sentence: He doesn't trust online reviews.
quests.hint: Doesn't fuses does and not into one word, sitting where does not would.
quests.explanation: Doesn't stands in for does not as a single word, right after He and before the base verb trust.

quests.sentence: We don't discuss salaries openly.
quests.hint: Don't is the contracted form for plural or I/you/we/they subjects, in the same position.
quests.explanation: Don't replaces do not as one word after We, with discuss in base form and openly (manner) closing the sentence.

quests.sentence: The system doesn't save changes automatically.
quests.hint: The contraction still comes right before the base verb, even with a manner adverb at the end.
quests.explanation: Doesn't precedes save, keeping the base verb form, while automatically (manner) closes the sentence in its usual end position.

quests.sentence: He did not attend the conference.
quests.hint: Did not carries all the past meaning, so the main verb returns to its base form.
quests.explanation: Did not follows He, and attend appears in base form instead of attended, since did already marks the past.

quests.sentence: They did not receive the invoice.
quests.hint: The same rule holds: did not plus the base verb, not the past-tense form.
quests.explanation: Did not precedes receive (base form, not received), following they, with the invoice as the object.

quests.sentence: The airline did not offer a refund.
quests.hint: A longer subject phrase doesn't change where did not sits or that the verb stays base form.
quests.explanation: Did not follows the airline, and offer stays base form, with a refund as the object.

quests.sentence: She didn't finish the presentation.
quests.hint: Didn't fuses did and not into one word, still followed by the base form of the verb.
quests.explanation: Didn't replaces did not as a single word before finish, which stays in base form after it.

quests.sentence: We didn't expect such a delay.
quests.hint: The same one-word contraction appears before expect, with the base verb form unchanged.
quests.explanation: Didn't precedes expect (base form), followed by the object such a delay, keeping the contracted-plus-base-verb pattern.

quests.sentence: The manager didn't approve the budget request.
quests.hint: Even with a compound object, didn't still sits right before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Didn't comes before approve (base form), and the budget request (a compound noun) completes the object.

quests.sentence: You cannot park here.
quests.hint: Cannot is written as one word and slots in right after the subject, before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Cannot follows You directly and precedes the base verb park — modal negatives keep the base verb form, just like do/does/did negatives.

quests.sentence: She should not ignore the warning.
quests.hint: Should not stays together as two words here, right after the subject and before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Should not follows She and precedes ignore (base form), with the warning as the object.

quests.sentence: We cannot guarantee immediate delivery.
quests.hint: Cannot still comes right after the subject, even with a two-word object at the end.
quests.explanation: Cannot follows We and precedes guarantee (base form), with immediate delivery as the object.

quests.sentence: I can't remember his name.
quests.hint: Can't fuses can and not into one word, staying right before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Can't replaces cannot informally, sitting before remember (base form), with his name as the object.

quests.sentence: You shouldn't skip breakfast.
quests.hint: Shouldn't is one word standing in for should not, in the same position before the base verb.
quests.explanation: Shouldn't precedes skip (base form) after You, showing the contracted modal keeps the same slot as its full form.

quests.sentence: She couldn't finish the marathon.
quests.hint: Couldn't works the same way, fusing could and not before the base verb finish.
quests.explanation: Couldn't comes before finish (base form) after She, with the marathon as the object.

quests.sentence: He was not aware of the change.
quests.hint: Was not works like is not, but for the past — not still follows the be-verb directly.
quests.explanation: Was not follows He and precedes aware, with of the change extending the complement — the past-tense counterpart to is not.

quests.sentence: They weren't satisfied with the service.
quests.hint: Weren't contracts were and not into one word, in the same position a full form would take.
quests.explanation: Weren't replaces were not as one unit after They, followed by satisfied and the extending phrase with the service.

quests.sentence: The summary wasn't accurate.
quests.hint: Wasn't works the same way for singular subjects, fusing was and not into one word.
quests.explanation: Wasn't stands in for was not after report, followed directly by the complement accurate.

quests.sentence: The manager wasn't able to attend the meeting.
quests.hint: Combine a be-negative contraction with an infinitive phrase — wasn't able, then to plus the base verb.
quests.explanation: Wasn't able to attend combines the past-be contraction wasn't with an infinitive verb pattern, followed by the meeting as the object.

quests.sentence: We don't usually work on weekends.
quests.hint: Mix a do-negative contraction with a mid-position frequency adverb, then close with a time expression.
quests.explanation: Don't (negative contraction) precedes usually (frequency, mid-position) and work (base verb), with on weekends (time) closing the sentence.

quests.sentence: She shouldn't ignore her doctor's advice.
quests.hint: Combine a modal-negative contraction with a possessive 's noun phrase as the object.
quests.explanation: Shouldn't precedes ignore (base form), and her doctor's advice (a possessive noun phrase) serves as the object, tying two earlier skills together.
